rationale: Module-boundary direct-callable replacements at the two observed encoder stage bundles, model.resnet.encoder.stages.0 (call ed609fcfe9f1b7538a7256aa) and stages.1 (call e4174ed71f25bb1aa98a4321), which share group 928c554228ed389eec5f plus every computational group fully contained in their subtrees. Previous feedback records the prior trial ACCEPTED, not a failure: the chunked-stem bundle (trial-4bdb465d41-param-0bfb4c5a) measured paired peak_allocated_bytes 204,905,472 vs original 281,975,808 (-27.3%) with images_per_second 7824-7986 above the 7120.31 floor, quality max_abs_error 0.0 on all 32,036 compared elements, zero framework fallbacks and empty candidate_diagnostics. So there is no concrete failure to repair; this attempt extends the measured-good pattern to the region the accepted evidence shows now sets the peak. Measured facts from that feedback and target-resources.json: the accepted parent's 204,905,472 B moment sits in stages.0.layers.1, where the live set is weights 46,758,048 + GPU-resident pixels 19,267,584 + stem output 25,690,112 + layers.0 output 25,690,112 + up to three more 25,690,112 B (32,64,56,56) temporaries inside conv2d->batch_norm->relu (~194.5 MB of live tensors plus ~10 MB conv workspace), while all later activations are <= 12,845,056 B per tensor. The secondary moment is stages.1.layers.0 (64->128 s2 transition with 1x1 stride-2 shortcut conv): pixels+weights+25.69 MB input + up to five 12,845,056 B (32,128,28,28) temporaries ~143 MB, which would become the new peak if only stages.0 were edited, so both stage calls in the shared group are replaced as one joint region. Replacement mechanics: at each stage boundary, stream the frozen batch through the identical parent aten operators (conv2d, eval batch_norm with training=False and frozen running stats, out-of-place relu, in-place residual add_ on chunk-owned temporaries, and for stages.1.layers.0 the 1x1 stride-2 shortcut conv+bn) in fixed sample chunks (default 8; 4 chunks for the frozen batch 32, remainder loop for any other batch) and copy each chunk result into one preallocated full-size output tensor. All these operators are strictly per-sample, so fixed-batch chunking is elementwise exact; CPU plumbing tests against the actual transformers 5.16.1 ResNetBasicLayer parent reproduce bitwise-identical outputs for every batch/chunk combination including remainders, both for the identity-shortcut and the conv-shortcut stage shape. Every physical aten site (30 sites: 9 conv2d, 9 batch_norm, 8 relu, 4 add_ across the two stages) executes through context['references'] per chunk, so the parent work keeps running and is counted on each invocation, exactly as the accepted stem bundle demonstrated (8 reference invocations per site, 88/88 kernels associated). No functional replacements are installed, so binding stays direct with no dispatch overhead on unrelated operators. Predicted warm-run peak_allocated_bytes: the stages.0 chunk moment becomes weights 46,758,048 + pixels 19,267,584 + chunked 25,690,112 input + 25,690,112 preallocated output + <=3 concurrent 6,422,528 B (8,64,56,56) temporaries ~136.7 MB plus small batch-8 conv workspace; the stages.1 chunk moment (~120.6 MB: 25.69 MB input + 12,845,056 B prealloc + <=5 x 3,211,264 B temporaries), the unedited stages.2 moment (~111 MB at (32,256,14,14)) and the installed stem moment (~116-117 MB) all stay below it, so the expected objective is ~140-150 MB versus the accepted 204,905,472 (-27% to -32%; ~-47% to -50% vs the original 281,975,808), to be measured by the paired evaluator. Throughput floor: current accepted latency 4.034 ms leaves ~460 us against the 4.4942 ms floor (images_per_second >= 7120.31). Added cost: ~38.5 MB of D2D chunk-result copies (~77 MB read+write traffic, ~85 us at the ~900 GB/s effective bandwidth observed in the diagnostic trace) and ~140 extra host launches, which the observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack (cuda_synchronize self 2.11 ms of 4.50 ms profiled wall) absorbs. GPU-side, the accepted stem evidence shows batch-8 implicit-GEMM convs cost 316.7 us total vs 268.0 us at batch 32 (+18%) while BN kernels dropped 227.7->75.2 us and relu 216.1->62.9 us (~3x faster); stages.0+stages.1 currently spend 1117.1+725.2 us with 900.1+612.3 us in convs and ~265 us in BN/relu/add, so the conv slowdown is expected to be largely offset by the elementwise/BN speedup, netting roughly neutral with ~300+ us of remaining headroom; one caveat is that stages.1's winograd conv kernels may re-key differently at batch-8 shapes. The declared chunk_samples parameter (choices 4/8/16) lets the frozen TaskSearch/TPE loop pick the memory/throughput point on this boundary without changing any task semantics (smaller chunks lower the chunk moment toward ~127-130 MB, larger chunks reduce launch count and conv inefficiency). Quality: logits expected within atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 and the +1-corruption control still rejected, verified by the frozen evaluator's repeated-forward closeness and top-1 checks in observe(). State lifecycle and synchronization: single process on one CUDA device, single stream, no collectives, nothing cached across invocations, no model parameters transformed, packed or copied; each invocation recomputes both stages from the live input tensor, reset()/models() semantics are untouched, and the returned tensors are freshly allocated contiguous fp32 CUDA tensors with the parent's exact shapes, so downstream stages and the classifier head remain valid consumers. stages.2/stages.3 stay deliberately outside the boundary: their eager moments (~104-111 MB) already sit below the post-edit floor set by the chunked stages.0 moment, so replacing them would add eliminated-call surface and launch overhead without moving the objective.
setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and allocates no device memory: it resolves the two stage parent callables from context['references'], the conv/batch-norm/relu/identity/shortcut modules from context['modules'] and the 30 aten operator references into Python closures, and verifies module types (Conv2d, BatchNorm2d with affine+running stats, out-of-place ReLU, Identity tails/shortcuts) once at installation; any mismatch only clears the ready flag so calls fall back to the parent under the setup_failure_parent label. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied, no CUDA Graph is captured, no global torch backend/math flag is touched (the evaluator's math_policy check stays green), and nothing is cached across invocations. Per-chunk temporaries (two to three 6,422,528 B (8,64,56,56) tensors in stages.0, up to five 3,211,264 B (8,128,28,28) tensors in stages.1) and the single preallocated full-size stage outputs (25,690,112 B and 12,845,056 B) are allocated inside each invocation through the caching allocator, so after warmup they are served from cached blocks and the setup receipt's allocated_bytes after installation remains the prepared model + pixels exactly as the parent. Retained allocator pools may come to include the 6.42/3.21 MB chunk block classes, so framework.reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peak counters can differ from the parent, while the objective framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per invocation and reflects only live allocations; the predicted decrease is specific to the warm-run peak_allocated_bytes counter of this workload, not a general physical-memory saving. The chunk size is read once from context['parameters']['chunk_samples'] (default 8; any non-positive or non-int value falls back to 8) and is fixed for the bundle installation.
quality_risks: Chunked conv2d runs cudnn's heuristic at the chunk batch size instead of batch 32 (cudnn.benchmark stays False). The implicit-GEMM family accumulates each output element over the same 3-tap or 9-tap reduction independently of the batch dimension, and the accepted stem bundle measured bitwise-identical logits (max_abs_error 0.0) with the same chunking; if a different algorithm were selected at stages.1's winograd-friendly shapes, per-element differences are fp32 round-off (~1e-6 relative), far below the frozen logits tolerance atol=rtol=1e-4 and immaterial to argmax margins. This remains the one numerics uncertainty and is left to the frozen evaluator's closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks.

Latency floor risk: ~38.5 MB of extra D2D copy traffic (~85 us), ~140 extra host launches (absorbed by the observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack) and possibly +18% conv time at batch-8 chunk shapes, partially offset by the measured ~3x speedup of the BN/relu kernels at smaller batch, against ~460 us of headroom on the 4.4942 ms floor; the chunk_samples parameter (4/8/16) is retunable by the frozen search inside the same boundary without changing semantics.

The 30 aten sites now execute with chunk-shaped signatures through context['references']; on the next discovery recapture they will be re-keyed under new call ids with chunk signatures (the framework recaptures the plan); consumers of the stage outputs still receive contiguous (32,64,56,56)/(32,128,28,28) fp32 CUDA tensors exactly as the parent produced.

Fallback labels keep the failure taxonomy observable: 'setup_failure_parent' (unresolved modules/references or module-type mismatch, including a replaced layer's shortcut no longer being Identity/conv+bn as assumed), 'unsupported_signature_parent' (guard mismatch, e.g. training mode, non-fp32/non-CUDA/non-contiguous tensors, wrong channel count, non-zeros padding, grouped conv) and 'runtime_failure_parent' (operator exception mid-composite, full parent recompute on the original input). The framework's signature guard additionally only dispatches the observed (32,64,56,56) stage calls to the replacements at all.

Memory accounting risk: the preallocated full-size stage output makes the new stages.0 moment (~136.7 MB) the expected peak, but allocator behavior (block reuse for the 25.69 MB input/output classes versus the retired full-size temporaries) can shift the measured counter a few MB in either direction; reserved pools may grow even as the per-invocation allocated peak falls, which is expected and not part of the objective.

params.name: chunk_samples
params.description: Fixed per-chunk sample count used to stream the frozen batch through the two observed stage boundaries. Every operator in the region (conv2d, eval batch_norm with frozen running stats, relu, residual add_, 1x1 stride-2 shortcut conv) is strictly per-sample, so any value yields elementwise-identical outputs; smaller chunks lower the chunk-temporary moment (~127-130 MB at 4) at the cost of more launches and lower conv efficiency, larger chunks trade memory for throughput. Read from context['parameters'] at build; default 8 when absent.

constraints.rationale: Legal chunk sizes for the frozen batch-32 workload; all choices divide 32, so the observed batch executes as equal chunks, and the remainder loop handles any other batch without changing frozen task semantics.

eliminated_calls_rationale: The whole computational subtrees inside model.resnet.encoder.stages.0 and stages.1 are replaced at the two stage boundaries, so the inner Python module calls no longer execute as module calls: the four ResNetBasicLayer bundles (74e9871b09ae9c4a1f947695, 7db3c2c1041bf3fe2951687e, 07e19be32b79aeb05aec13d6, 5317ed169e344be620e52d7e), their layer Sequentials and ResNetConvLayers, the nine Conv2d modules, the nine BatchNorm2d modules, the eight ReLU modules, the seven Identity modules (activation tails and identity shortcuts) and the stages.1.layers.0 ResNetShortCut. Their computational content is preserved exactly: the replacements read the same live module parameters (conv weights/strides/paddings, BN affine and frozen running stats, eps/momentum) and execute the equivalent aten operators through context['references'] on every invocation; only the intermediate Python module boundaries and the full-resolution (32,64,56,56)/(32,128,28,28) temporaries they materialized are gone, replaced by chunk-shaped temporaries plus one preallocated output per stage. The aten conv2d/batch_norm/relu/add_ sites themselves are NOT eliminated (they keep executing through references and were excluded from this list). The profiler record_function enter/exit entries are discovery instrumentation markers around the captured ops, not computational work; their consumers are trace analysis only, and the framework's recapture will emit fresh markers for the chunked path. The only consumers of the eliminated calls' outputs are the two stages themselves, which return the same contiguous full-size fp32 CUDA tensors to the encoder loop, the later stages and the classification head, so all downstream consumers remain valid.
